outcome: Still open as of 13 Oct 2026, but the best upper bound moved in September 2026: Keller (arXiv 2609.21968, 18 Sep 2026, AI-assisted, Lean 4 formalisation claimed, unrefereed) gives a convex universal cover of area ≈ 0.2463322, which also bounds the unrestricted minimum from above; Deng (arXiv 2609.04591, 4 Sep 2026, unrefereed) claims an unrestricted isosceles-triangle cover of area ≈ 0.2578836; the lower bounds found in the literature are for convex covers only and last moved in 2011 (0.232239) and, for convex covers, in 2026 (0.239, Keller).
problem_asks: The statement asks for M, the infimum (smallest) area of a planar set S such that every curve of unit length has a congruent copy inside S. Unpacked: (a) the value of M; (b) whether a set attaining M exists (not known in general, per Wikipedia; existence for convex covers follows from Blaschke selection, as stated in the Wikipedia article and Laidacker–Poole); (c) which shape attains M, i.e. its identity. The bullet does not restrict S to convex sets and does not restrict curves to arcs or closed curves; the standard reading (Wikipedia, Norwood–Poole) takes ‘curve’ as a rectifiable arc, allows rotation and translation, and excludes reflections. Convex-only and closed-curve versions are different questions and are recorded as such below. The claim is universal over all unit-length curves, not over finitely many.

events.what_happened: Ethan Keller (sole author), arXiv:2609.21968 (math.MG, cross-list cs.CG), ‘Improved bounds for universal convex covers of unit arcs’, one version. Claims that α, the infimum area of a convex universal cover of unit arcs, satisfies 0.239 ≤ α ≤ 7170601298323360123534337/29109471743520000000000000 = 0.2463322372…, reducing the gap between the previous refereed bounds (0.232239 and π/12) by over 75%. Lower bound: four explicit unit polygonal arcs and a finite subdivision certified with shoelace bounds. Upper bound: a quadrilateral with rational data, shown to cover every unit arc by a finite case tree of support and length inequalities. Author states the proofs are formalised in Lean 4 with mathlib, code and certificates at github.com/ethan-keller/moser-worm-improved-bounds (Apache-2.0). Paper states it was AI-assisted (see ai).
events.revisions: v1 only (Fri 18 Sep 2026 16:29:55 UTC); no later version found as of 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Upper bound: M ≤ α ≤ 0.2463322…, for the unrestricted minimum M as well, because every convex cover is a cover (M ≤ M_conv is a logical consequence, since every convex cover is a cover; Deng 2609.04591 states the same inequality). Lower bound: α ≥ 0.239 for convex covers only. A lower bound on the convex infimum does not bound the unrestricted M from below. Restrictions: convex covers; unit arcs (the paper does not treat closed curves).
events.remains: (a) The exact value of M: open. The paper says the quadrilateral ‘has not been proved optimal’ and that a matching lower bound would be needed. (b) Existence of a minimiser: not addressed. (c) Identity of a minimiser: not identified. Unrestricted lower bound: not addressed by this event.

events.what_happened: Zhipeng Deng (sole author), arXiv:2609.04591, ‘Balanced Support Calibrations for Moser’s Worm Problem: Exact Certificate and Bound of Triangular Cover’, one version (49 pp; comments: ‘Lean 4 code for formal proofs, and Python code for exact symbolic replay verifier’). Claims that an isosceles triangle T with equal sides 1, base angles β with tan β = 766/197, has D⁻¹T containing a congruent copy of every rectifiable planar unit arc (Corollary 7.2), where D = 82074390584/84861020075 is a rational lower bound E(T) ≥ D obtained from three exhaustive branches, so the cover ratio area(T)/D² = 11511821678274125/44639604443512928 ≈ 0.2578835951. The paper states the bound for the unrestricted problem, not just convex covers.

events.remains: (a) Exact M: not determined. (b) Existence of a minimiser: not addressed. (c) Identity of a minimiser: not identified. No lower bound for M in this event.

events.directly_checkable: The triangle is explicit: vertices (−c, 0), (c, 0), (0, s) with c = 197/√625565 and s = 766/√625565, so c² + s² = 1 (equal sides 1). Base 2c ≈ 0.498, height s ≈ 0.968, area cs = 150902/625565. Cover ratio area(T)/D² with the rational D above. The paper’s Python replay verifier checks 512 one-delimiter and 4096 two-delimiter orders in exact rational arithmetic. I did not run it.
events.doubts: (1) Single author; no human engagement found. (2) The paper itself states that the global planar Λ-configuration theorem and the compactness bookkeeping are ‘explicit hypotheses or ordinary mathematical arguments’, and that generated rational interval and rectangle data are excluded from the Lean file, so the Lean file does not by itself cover the whole chain. (3) The decisive numerical check is an exact Python replay, not a Lean proof. (4) I did not read the three branches of the exhaustive analysis. (5) Keller (18 Sep 2026) cites this as an unrefereed preprint and quotes the number; that is a citation, not a check.
events.direction: Upper bound moves down on the unrestricted problem: from 0.260437 (Norwood–Poole 2003) or 0.26007 (Ploymaklam–Wichiramala 2018, second-hand) to 0.2578836, if the claim holds. Not a counterexample; no lower bound.
events.object: An explicit isosceles triangle with base angles β, tan β = 766/197 (about 75.58°), equal sides 1, base 394/√625565 ≈ 0.498 and height 766/√625565 ≈ 0.968. The claim is that a homothetic copy scaled by 1/D with D ≈ 0.967162 contains a copy of every rectifiable unit arc. The covering argument is exact rational interval arithmetic over three exhaustive branches plus a stated planar configuration hypothesis; not non-constructive.

events.what_happened: Chatchawan Panraksa and Wacharin Wichiramala, arXiv:2606.14625, ‘Wetzel’s 30°-60°-90° Triangle Covers Unit Arcs’, one version (68 pp, 16 figs). Claims that the 30-60-90 triangle T with a square of side 1/3 on the hypotenuse covers every unit arc, by a computer-assisted proof: a hypothetical uncovered arc reduces to 599 closed second-order cone models, each certified by interval validation of stored dual certificates (Mathematica 10.4 and 12.3 with an SOCP solver). Since every certified lower endpoint exceeds 1.0048, the homothetic copy T/1.0048 covers every unit arc and has area ≈ 0.260956. Code and certificates at github.com/chatchawanpan-dev/wetzel-triangle-computation (referenced, not opened).
events.delivers: Convex upper bound: α_conv ≤ 0.260956…, improving π/12 ≈ 0.261799 for convex covers; hence M ≤ 0.260956…. This does not improve the unrestricted upper bound already in the literature (0.26007 or 0.260437), which is smaller. Also, per the authors, settles Wetzel’s triangle conjecture. Restrictions: a convex (triangular) cover of unit arcs.
events.remains: (a) Exact M: not determined. (b) Existence of a minimiser: not addressed. (c) Identity of a minimiser: not identified. No lower bound in this event.

disputes.summary: The unrestricted (nonconvex) record is given as 0.260437 (Norwood–Poole 2003; Wikipedia, Deng 2608, Deng 2609) and as ≈ 0.26007 (Ploymaklam–Wichiramala 2018; Deng 2609 and the Vertu article’s baseline of 0.2600697). I did not reconcile these; the Ploymaklam value is second-hand only. The convex lower bound is given as 0.227498 in some sources and 0.232239 in others; the latter is the later value (2011). Wikipedia’s summary of the 2026 status conflicts with the arXiv listings I read; the Wikipedia page was last edited 2 April 2026 and did not mention 2026 preprints in the text I read.

Publication year of Panraksa–Wichiramala’s sector paper is 2020 in one source (online, DOI 10.1007/s10998-020-00354-x) and 2021 in another (volume 82(2)); the Wikipedia article gives 2021. The arXiv date (17 Jul 2019) is the one used here.

summary: The problem is still open on 13 Oct 2026, but the upper bound moved in September 2026 and the record is thin. Keller (arXiv 2609.21968, 18 Sep 2026; sole author; unrefereed; only an automated Pith review) proves 0.239 ≤ α ≤ 0.2463322… for convex universal covers of unit arcs, using a Lean 4 formalisation that the author says is sorry-free (I read the paper’s own description and the README, not the Lean sources). Because every convex cover is a cover, the upper bound also bounds the unrestricted minimum: it lowers the record from 0.260437 (or 0.26007) to 0.2463322. The lower bound 0.239 is for convex covers only and does not bound the unrestricted minimum from below. The Acknowledgments say generative AI tools (named as Claude Opus and Fable families, GPT-5 family and Astra, through Claude Code, Codex and web chat) were used, and that they ‘carried out the exploration, the discovery of the geometric reductions’ and the Lean formalisation; the author says they ‘reviewed and verified all AI-generated output’. This is the only event I found where the authors credit AI systems with load-bearing mathematics, and the quotes are the authors’ own; they come from a summarising fetch of the HTML, not a character-checked copy. Deng (arXiv 2609.04591, 4 Sep 2026; sole author; unrefereed) claims an isosceles triangle with cover ratio 0.2578835951… covering every rectifiable unit arc, for the unrestricted problem; the paper’s own Lean scope is partial and the decisive check is an exact Python replay I did not run; no AI statement appears in the text I read. Wichiramala and Panraksa (arXiv 2606.14625, 12 Jun 2026) give a convex triangle cover of area 0.260956, computer-assisted with interval certificates; this beats the convex record π/12 but not the unrestricted 0.26007. Deng 2608.01393 (Aug 2026) gives only a conditional worm bound from a numerical optimum, and Deng 2412.10686 (Dec 2024) extends a Bellman-problem method to the worm without a number. A lifestyle article (Vertu, 15 Jan 2026) reports, from an unlinked Reddit post, that OpenAI’s ‘5.2 Pro’ shaved about 2×10⁻⁷ off a shape-family area (0.2600697 to 0.2600695); it names no author, and there is no author-level account, so I did not place ‘5.2 Pro’ in ai.systems and treat the claim as unverified. Lower bounds for convex covers are 0.227498 (2007), 0.232239 (2011, journal 2013) and 0.239 (Keller 2026); no lower bound for the unrestricted minimum appeared in any source I opened, and a secondary source attributes a 0.21946 lower bound to Wetzel (undated, not verified). Close calls: (i) whether a convex-only lower bound, or an upper bound from a convex cover, counts as moving ‘the smallest area of a shape’ depends on how the judging pass reads the statement’s unrestricted wording; (ii) whether a computer-assisted triangle result or a Lean-formalised result counts as more reliable is a judgement I have left to the later pass. Searches for lab announcements (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic), AlphaEvolve, a Tao post, an ‘AI tracker’ and Reddit threads returned nothing bearing on this problem beyond the Vertu report.
competing_reading: Keller’s quadrilateral is a valid convex cover, so the unrestricted upper bound moved to 0.2463322 with a Lean-checked proof and an AI-assisted process that the authors describe. On that reading the problem’s upper-bound status moved substantially in September 2026, and the AI involvement is load-bearing. The opposite reading: the paper is a single-author, AI-assisted, unrefereed preprint whose only human-visible check is an automated AI referee; its lower bound is for convex covers only and so changes a different quantity; the Deng triangle is unrefereed and its Lean file excludes stated parts; and the Vertu result is unverified. Under that reading the problem has moved only in unreviewed preprints, with no settled change to the value of M.
what_would_settle_it: For Keller: a Lean-literate audit of the statement MoserWorm.bounds (does it formalise ‘every unit arc has a congruent copy in K’ with the right notion of congruence, and is the sorry status true across the repository?), plus a referee or expert check of the lower-bound subdivision and the upper-bound case tree; and a note on which model did which step, since the paper names families, not versions. For Deng 2609.04591: an independent check of the three exhaustive branches and of the planar configuration hypothesis the paper leaves outside Lean. For Wichiramala–Panraksa 2606.14625: an independent run of the 599 certificate checks. For the Vertu claim: the original Reddit post, its author and a paper or post by the named verifier. For the unrestricted lower bound: any paper giving a positive lower bound for covers that are not assumed convex.

event.what_happened: Zhipeng Deng (sole author), arXiv:2609.04591, ‘Balanced Support Calibrations for Moser’s Worm Problem: Exact Certificate and Bound of Triangular Cover’, one version (49 pp; comments: ‘Lean 4 code for formal proofs, and Python code for exact symbolic replay verifier’). Claims that an isosceles triangle T with equal sides 1, base angles β with tan β = 766/197, has D⁻¹T containing a congruent copy of every rectifiable planar unit arc (Corollary 7.2), where D = 82074390584/84861020075 is a rational lower bound E(T) ≥ D obtained from three exhaustive branches, so the cover ratio area(T)/D² = 11511821678274125/44639604443512928 ≈ 0.2578835951. The paper states the bound for the unrestricted problem, not just convex covers.
event.revisions: v1 only (Fri 4 Sep 2026 00:46:13 UTC). One search summary gave 3 Sep; arXiv’s UTC stamp is 4 Sep.
event.delivers: Upper bound on the unrestricted M: M ≤ 0.2578835951…, by an explicit isosceles triangle (convex, so it also bounds the convex infimum). No lower bound. Restrictions: the claimed cover rests on the author’s exhaustive-branch argument with rational interval data; the stated Lean scope is partial (see doubts).
event.remains: (a) Exact M: not determined. (b) Existence of a minimiser: not addressed. (c) Identity of a minimiser: not identified. No lower bound for M in this event.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib (per the author’s statement in Appendix C and §10.1); Python exact symbolic replay verifier (Appendix D)

event.directly_checkable: The triangle is explicit: vertices (−c, 0), (c, 0), (0, s) with c = 197/√625565 and s = 766/√625565, so c² + s² = 1 (equal sides 1). Base 2c ≈ 0.498, height s ≈ 0.968, area cs = 150902/625565. Cover ratio area(T)/D² with the rational D above. The paper’s Python replay verifier checks 512 one-delimiter and 4096 two-delimiter orders in exact rational arithmetic. I did not run it.
event.doubts: (1) Single author; no human engagement found. (2) The paper itself states that the global planar Λ-configuration theorem and the compactness bookkeeping are ‘explicit hypotheses or ordinary mathematical arguments’, and that generated rational interval and rectangle data are excluded from the Lean file, so the Lean file does not by itself cover the whole chain. (3) The decisive numerical check is an exact Python replay, not a Lean proof. (4) I did not read the three branches of the exhaustive analysis. (5) Keller (18 Sep 2026) cites this as an unrefereed preprint and quotes the number; that is a citation, not a check.
event.direction: Upper bound moves down on the unrestricted problem: from 0.260437 (Norwood–Poole 2003) or 0.26007 (Ploymaklam–Wichiramala 2018, second-hand) to 0.2578836, if the claim holds. Not a counterexample; no lower bound.
event.object: An explicit isosceles triangle with base angles β, tan β = 766/197 (about 75.58°), equal sides 1, base 394/√625565 ≈ 0.498 and height 766/√625565 ≈ 0.968. The claim is that a homothetic copy scaled by 1/D with D ≈ 0.967162 contains a copy of every rectifiable unit arc. The covering argument is exact rational interval arithmetic over three exhaustive branches plus a stated planar configuration hypothesis; not non-constructive.

events.credibility_reason: The paper itself leaves the global planar configuration theorem and compactness steps outside Lean as stated hypotheses or informal arguments; decisive check is a Python replay; no human engagement.
Worm bound is conditional on an uncertified numerical optimum; no explicit area stated.
Secondary lifestyle site only; no primary post, author, paper or named verifier; shape family unidentified; internally inconsistent; claimed gain at the rounding level of the baseline figure.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the minimum area over all (not necessarily convex) covers of unit curves, so only events that lower the unrestricted upper bound or raise an unrestricted lower bound count as bound; convex-only, closed-curve and convex-arc results, and convex covers that do not beat the existing unrestricted record (Panraksa–Wichiramala 2019 and 2026, Wang 2006, Wichiramala 2005 for convex arcs), are variants. Keller's quadrilateral lowers the unrestricted upper bound to 0.2463 (its 0.239 lower bound is convex-only), so it is a bound; its Lean build and the Pith AI review are not digestion. Its AI role is generated rather than assisted: the author's own acknowledgments say the models carried out the exploration, discovered the geometric reductions and developed the proofs, with the author steering and verifying, which is AI producing the mathematics with human checking. Deng's triangle also lowers the unrestricted bound and is kept as doubtful because the paper itself leaves key steps outside its formal check. The Vertu report is set aside: no primary source, no named author or verifier, unidentified shape.
judgement.doubts: Keller's AI quotes come from a summarising fetch, not a character-checked copy, and do not say which model did what, so all four named families are credited; if the wording were weaker, assisted would be the reading. Whether Keller's quadrilateral is generated or assisted is the close call. Ploymaklam–Wichiramala 2018 value and venue are second-hand.
